**Finding submitted: needs_review (INDEMN).**

Summary of the review:

- **What exists.** Article 11 is a reciprocal indemnity architecture. Section 11.2 (p0560) has Harpoon — the counterparty — expressly indemnify *and defend* AbbVie, its Affiliates and their directors/officers/employees/agents against Third Party Claims. Sections 11.3 (notice), 11.4.1/11.4.2 (assumption and control of defence, with our right to participate and to control where interests are adverse), and 11.4.4 (cooperation) supply the full standard procedure. Four preferred elements are therefore already met on verbatim text, and this is clearly not walk-away territory (it is not a one-way Customer indemnity).

- **Why I did not clear it as compliant.** The operative trigger lists of *both* 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted (`arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]`). The substance the rule cares about — IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused data breach, Harpoon's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and whether *our* 11.1 indemnity stays narrow — is simply not on the page. Section 7.4 and p0471 point toward some IP coverage ("Subject to Section 11.2"; "a claim that may be subject to Section 11.2"), but that is inference from a cross-reference, not operative language.

- **Why I did not redline.** Drafting inserts against a redacted trigger list would risk duplicating or contradicting terms the parties have already agreed. The shortest correct next step is to obtain the unredacted 11.1/11.2 triggers and confirm Harpoon IP-infringement coverage and the narrowness of our reciprocal indemnity.

- **Noted, not flagged:** Article 11 carries no monetary super-cap, and 11.5's mutual consequential-damages exclusion expressly carves out third-party amounts payable under an Article 11 indemnity — that carve-out runs in our favour.
